content: Simulation vs reality gaps (FoundationDB/Antithesis/Tigerbeetle practice): idealized fault models miss gray failures, asymmetric routing, kernel buffer drops (SO_RCVBUF overflow), IP-fragmentation loss amplification, NIC/driver quirks; a single simulation run explores a tiny fraction of event traces - need randomized fault schedules, many seeds; simulator must intercept ALL external interactions (network, disk, time) for determinism. Simulation passes do not substitute for a real-socket smoke test (quickstart two-nodes-on-localhost) because real stacks add own-broadcast echo, per-interface duplicates, and buffer drops the virtual network may not model.
